editorial:
Imagine finding out a wealthy relative just passed away, but instead of grieving, everyone in the house starts acting like sharks in a tank. That is exactly what happens when Fujishima Motoharu, the head of a solid mid-sized company, dies suddenly. You get to watch his family members transform from loving relatives into greedy strangers as they fight over who gets the money and the business. The vibe is tense and sneaky, making you feel like you are eavesdropping on private arguments behind closed doors. You will find yourself wondering who to root for, or if any of them even deserve a single penny.

What really makes this work is how the tension builds up slowly until it finally boils over. The acting is top-notch because the actors play the greed so realistically that you might actually get annoyed with them. While the pace is a bit slower than a modern thriller, the twists make it worth your time. If you enjoy family dramas with a dark side, you should definitely give this a go. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, the battle for the money reveals that the family members cared more about the cash than the man who died. The big twist shows that Motoharu knew exactly how greedy they were before he passed. He left a will that basically tricks them or strips them of the power they fought for. It wraps up with the family left in shock, realizing their greed cost them everything in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about greedy families and secret wills.
